asr.full_text: Time is money If you are already a member, this is a video you must watch. The mission of Merit Trading International is to grow your bitcoin. The value of one bitcoin could be between $500,000 and $1,000,000 by the year 2030. We would like you to be responsible and check your back office regularly. Here's why. Look for any amount in either the Activation Wallet or income wallet. If you have bitcoin in either of these accounts, please realize this money is not working for you. The only place your bitcoin can work for you is in the Trading Pool account. The other place your bitcoin can work is if you withdraw your money and pay debt so that you ultimately become debt-free. Here are the steps for moving bitcoin from the Activation Wall wallet to the Pool account. Click on the Pool account, then add funds to Pool in the left hand menu. A screen will open which has a heading Add Fund to trading pool. All you need to do is click submit. Once you have clicked submit you will get a notification, Thank you! Funds successfully added to Pool Account. You can go to your back office and confirm your balance has increased by the amount that was in your Activation Wallet. When you look at the Income Wallet, you will see the Includes Pending Bonuses, Click on that and you will get a list of all your pending bonuses and binary bonuses if you have qualified. Remember that all bonuses have a list of all the bonuses as you have qualified. All bonuses have a 7-day waiting period. The list will indicate the days, hours and minutes to release. To move your bitcoins from your income wallet to your Pool account, click on the wallet section on the left-hand menu. Then click Internal Fund Transfer. See exactly what is available and what is still pending. section on the left-hand menu and then click internal fund transfer here you can see exactly what is available and what is still pending now select the option you want which will be the income to trading pool wallet now into the Bitcoin amount you would like to transfer and enter your login password click submit then a new screen will come up and you can click confirm. Once you confirm, you will receive a notification saying amount transferred successfully. You can go the your backoffice and confirm that your balance has increased by the amount that was transferred. Should you have any questions, please contact your team leader.

textual.observation: The source claims that bitcoin can grow or work for the audience in a Trading Pool account and instructs members to move bitcoin from other wallets into that account.

evidence.quote: The mission of Merit Trading International is to grow your bitcoin.
The only place your bitcoin can work for you is in the Trading Pool account.
Here are the steps for moving bitcoin from the Activation Wall wallet to the Pool account.

textual.context: Promotional and instructional context directed at existing members; the source also presents debt repayment as an alternative use of withdrawn funds.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised bitcoin-growth or return claim is directly linked to a requested transfer of bitcoin into the Trading Pool account.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish whether the trading pool exists, whether bitcoin is actually invested or grows, who controls the destination, or whether any loss occurred.

textual.observation: The transfer procedure instructs the audience to enter a login password before confirming an internal bitcoin transfer.

evidence.quote: now into the Bitcoin amount you would like to transfer and enter your login password click submit

textual.context: Presented as routine account instructions for transferring funds within the described platform; whether this is a normal authentication step is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: A request to provide or enter account credentials is linked to an internal transfer of bitcoin.
textual.limitations: The records do not show where the password is entered, whether it is transmitted to another party, whether credentials are exposed, or whether the transfer is authorized.

visual.observation: A presentation slide displays “Value 1 Bitcoin 2030” and “$500,000 - $1,000,000” alongside Mirror Trading International branding.
visual.context: The claim appears in a branded presentation; whether it is a forecast, promise, quotation, or other context is unclear from the sampled frame.
visual.potential_relevance: A stated future monetary return is associated with the promoted trading organization, which may merit review of the claim and its connection to the organization.
visual.limitations: The frame does not establish whether the amount is guaranteed, conditional, representative, or actually attainable, and does not show a requested action or transaction outcome.

visual.observation: A member dashboard labeled “Paid Member” shows team-member and direct-referral counts, multiple BTC bonus categories, trading-pool balances, and an “Activation Wallet Balance.”
visual.context: The interface visibly presents itself as a paid-member account dashboard and displays referral and bonus information.
visual.potential_relevance: The combination of paid membership, recruitment-related counts, and bonus/trading-pool balances shows a relationship between account participation, referrals, and stated monetary benefits.
visual.limitations: The sampled dashboard does not show membership fees, referral instructions, withdrawal results, or whether the displayed balances represent real funds.

visual.observation: The interface opens “Add Funds To Trading Pool” and shows an amount field, a user ID field, payment through an “Activation Wallet Balance,” and a Submit button.
visual.context: The frames depict an account workflow for adding funds to a trading pool; one frame displays a success message stating “Thank you. Funds successfully sent to pool account.”
visual.potential_relevance: A requested funding action is visibly connected to an activation-wallet balance and a trading-pool account, creating a concrete money-flow relationship relevant to review alongside the displayed bonus and return claims.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish the source, recipient, authorization status, or external outcome of the funds, and the sampled sequence cannot independently prove that a submission or transfer occurred.

visual.observation: A slide states “Trading Pool” and “Withdraw - Pay your Debts” next to Mirror Trading International branding.
visual.context: This is a branded presentation slide; the wording may be an instruction, description, quotation, or slogan, and the surrounding context is unclear.
visual.potential_relevance: The slide associates a trading pool with withdrawal-related use of funds, which may merit review of what return or access to funds is being represented.
visual.limitations: The frame does not show withdrawal conditions, an actual withdrawal, debt details, or whether the statement is directed at viewers.

visual.observation: An “Internal Fund Transfer” form displays BTC wallet balances, an amount-in-bitcoin field, and a transaction-password field; a later frame displays “Amount transferred successfully.”
visual.context: The frames show an apparent internal transfer workflow between income and trading-pool wallets, followed by an on-screen success message.
visual.potential_relevance: The workflow requests entry of a bitcoin amount and transaction password to move funds into a trading-pool wallet, linking credential submission and asset transfer to the trading-pool system.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames cannot verify whether the password was entered correctly, whether a transfer occurred externally, or who controlled the destination wallet.

visual_context_notes.observation: The sampled material uses Mirror Trading International branding and includes a dashboard marked “Paid Member,” referral/team sections, and bitcoin balance displays.
The final sampled slide directs viewers to “Please contact your Team Leader.”

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it tells Mirror Trading International members that Bitcoin can 'work' only after transfer into MTI's Trading Pool, an investment program later found fraudulent by a federal court in a CFTC case. The walkthrough moves BTC from activation or income balances to the pool, while the dashboard also advertises referral and binary bonuses; it is an instruction to commit funds to that scheme, not an independent investigation.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S03 is primary because the requested act is transferring Bitcoin into MTI's claimed trading pool for growth. S06 is secondary because the shown team, direct-referral and binary-bonus fields document the program's recruitment layer; the CFTC finding is separate external context.

evidence.observation: The narration directs viewers to place Bitcoin in a trading pool as the place where it can generate value.
evidence.quote: The only place your bitcoin can work for you is in the Trading Pool account.

evidence.observation: The narration claims that transferring Bitcoin from the activation wallet increases the back-office balance.
evidence.quote: You can go to your back office and confirm your balance has increased by the amount that was in your Activation Wallet.

evidence.observation: The dashboard visibly shows Total Team Members, Direct Referrals, Left Team, Right Team, Binary Bonuses, and Trading Bonuses.
The pending bonus history visibly labels the entry as Referral Bonus.
The transfer instructions explicitly ask the member to enter a login password.
